speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry is studying how effective subject-based banding, where secondary school students learn each subject at the level that best caters to their strengths, interests and learning needs, has been on social mixing in schools; (b) if so, what are the Ministry’s findings so far; and (c) if not, whether the Ministry will start studying this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Education)
text: School leaders and teachers also observed that their students are taking greater ownership of their learning and are more motivated to overcome challenges they face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We are heartened to see the early positive outcomes arising from the hard work by school leaders and teachers in implementing Full SBB, with the support of parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just check specifically what indicators MOE is looking at in terms of studying the extent of social mixing as a result of SBB?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned about increasing resources to the schools.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I check exactly what additional resources are provided to the teachers to help them with this?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: On the Member's first question, there are several indicators.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: So, that is one of the key indicators.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: The rest are qualitative in terms of emotional feedback and surveys on how they find certain networks are useful.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: On the Member's second question, for example, for Full SBB, obviously, there is a more diverse curriculum and there are more movements.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Schedules will definitely be a lot more robust and dynamic.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: That, certainly, has increased some of the workload and, invariably, teachers and schools will have to manage that.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: So, one way that we are doing it is looking at artificial intelligence, and technology and capability in how we can better do scheduling so that distance and travels will be less, less dynamism within the form classes and so on, so that there will be more time for the form teachers to spend time with some of their form class students as well.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: It is slightly different, but we are monitoring that and we are getting feedback, and we will see what are some of the key technologies or processes that we can implement cohort-wide that could be accretive to this group.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: On the topic of social capital and social network diversity, can I ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary that for these studies, will MOE look at it much further into the future?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: That means looking at the cohort, not just as they progress through school but to the end of formal schooling, and even into the early years of working life, so that we can see how this lifts up children, not just at age 18, but even at 28 or 38 in the years ahead?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: There will be a review every now and then, and we will most certainly provide updates then.
